copies.headline: Noah's Roster Finally Outruns His Scoreboard
copies.body:
Noah is 0-2 with 84.7 a game, dead last in points and 2-20 in all-play, which is a genuinely impressive way to be the better team on paper. The backfield is the reason: De'Von Achane and James Cook III are worth about nine over Grant's best pair, and Cook has the friendliest script on the slate with Buffalo laying seven in a 50.5. Achane's game is uglier — Miami as a 10.5-point dog against Kansas City is a lot of empty second-half targets, but that chase-mode volume is exactly how he gets there. Grant's answer is Omarion Hampton plus a questionable Jadarian Price and a questionable Tony Pollard, which is depth in name only.
Grant's edge is real and it's at receiver: Amon-Ra St. Brown in a 47.5 home game against the Jets, Zay Flowers in a 52.5 in Dallas, Christian Watson. That's eleven points of cushion, and it needs to hold, because Juwan Johnson at tight end with Dallas Goedert doubtful is a hole, and Kyler Murray in a 42.5 grinder at Tampa isn't bailing anyone out. Noah's third receiver is Josh Downs or Michael Wilson, which is thin, but Mike Evans clearing questionable against Arizona shrinks the gap fast.

copies.headline: Isaac's Receivers Can't Carry This Alone
copies.body:
Isaac's one real edge is the wideout room — Ja'Marr Chase, Terry McLaurin, DK Metcalf and a questionable Malik Nabers get him +5 on CJ's top three — and even that comes with tags attached. Nabers and Jakobi Meyers are both listed, and Chase's Bengals game at Pittsburgh has a 42.5 total in a spot where Cincinnati is favored and may just lean on the run. Everywhere else it's CJ: +2 at quarterback with Tyler Shough at home against Las Vegas, +5 at running back behind Jonathan Taylor, and a deeper bench with Chuba Hubbard and Quinshon Judkins as real flex answers. Isaac's back three is three guys, and Jaylen Warren is questionable.
The season splits say the same thing louder. CJ is 3rd in scoring at 126.4 and 14-8 all-play; Isaac is 89.6 a week, 5-17 all-play, and hasn't cracked 90 yet. That 1-1 record is charity. The one path is Chase and Metcalf going nuclear in a division game while Taylor gets bottled up by Houston in a 42.5-total slog — plausible, not likely, and Isaac has no floor underneath it if it doesn't hit.

copies.headline: Kaleb's Backfield Outweighs John's Tight End Math
copies.body:
The running backs decide this. Kaleb rolls out Ashton Jeanty and Breece Hall for 35 projected against John's 25, and the gap is worse than it reads: Jeanty gets New Orleans in a 43.5-total game where Vegas grinds, and Hall is attached to a Jets team getting 6.5 in Detroit, which means volume late. John's best two are D'Andre Swift and Kyren Williams at 13 apiece, and Blake Corum is sitting right behind Kyren siphoning goal-line work in a Rams game they're only favored by 2.5 to win. RJ Harvey is questionable for Kaleb but he's the RB3, not the plan.
John's path is Trey McBride plus a healthy Puka Nacua, and he needs both. Nacua is questionable, Brock Bowers is questionable, and Caleb Williams is doubtful behind Matthew Stafford — that's three coin flips on a roster with no margin. Kaleb's receiver room is deeper and safer: London, McConkey in a 50.5-total shootout at Buffalo, plus Addison and Tate as real replacements. John scored 159.5 then 81.7. That variance cuts both ways, and Kaleb only needs the floor.

copies.headline: Leif's Receivers Can't Cover Adam's Spread
copies.body:
The top two teams in scoring and all-play meet, and it comes down to one position. Adam's best three receivers project 52 to Leif's 33, a 19-point hole that Josh Allen's three-point edge over Brock Purdy and a two-point RB bump don't come close to filling. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the centerpiece of a Seattle offense favored by seven, Chris Olave gets Las Vegas in a game New Orleans should control, and Adam still has Rome Odunze and a questionable Jalen Coker behind them. Leif's WR3 is Caleb Douglas or Rashod Bateman. That's not a room, that's a waiting list.
Leif's counterpunch is real: McCaffrey against Arizona in a 47.5, Derrick Henry in a 52.5 at Dallas, and Allen at home laying seven in the week's highest-scoring environment. But Kenneth Walker gets Miami with Kansas City favored by 10.5 — script city — and Bucky Irving sees volume as a slight underdog. Adam's floor is the highest in the league for a reason.

copies.headline: Christian's Depth Buries Mitchell's Question Marks
copies.body:
Somebody has to win, and the roster math says it's Christian. His receiver room is the difference: CeeDee Lamb in a 52.5-total game against Baltimore, DeVonta Smith, Deebo Samuel, plus Jameson Williams and Khalil Shakir in a 50.5-point Bills game as the fifth option. Mitchell's top three go 40 with two questionable tags on the best two — Nico Collins in a 42.5-total slog at Indianapolis and DJ Moore, who's third in line in Buffalo. If either sits, Mitchell is starting Matthew Golden and Courtland Sutton and hoping.
Mitchell's edge is Jahmyr Gibbs against the Jets, and that's real — Detroit laying 6.5 in a 47.5 game is exactly the script where he gets 20 touches. But behind Gibbs it's Rachaad White and a day-to-day Josh Jacobs, while Christian can roll Chase Brown, Kamara and Tuten. Add Darnold questionable in Seattle's 40.5-total road game, and Mitchell needs two boom weeks to a Christian floor that's already 125 a game.

copies.headline: Logan's 0-2 Is A Lie, Peter's 2-0 Is Too
copies.body:
The receiver room decides this. Logan can start Justin Jefferson, Tetairoa McMillan and any of four 11-point bodies, and Peter counters with George Pickens, Tee Higgins and Romeo Doubs — a six-point gap that widens once you notice Peter's WR4 is Denzel Boston and his WR5 is Jalen McMillan. A.J. Brown is on IR and nothing replaces him. Peter's edge is exactly one point at quarterback, and Lamar Jackson in a 52.5-total game in Dallas is the single best reason he wins. Pickens is in that same game, which is Peter's whole ceiling: Cowboys chasing, throwing late.
Running back is closer than the depth chart suggests. Saquon Barkley is questionable and Philadelphia is favored in a 41.5 game, the kind they close out on the ground, but Logan has Jeremiyah Love, Tyler Allgeier and Braelon Allen behind him. Peter has Bijan Robinson in a 42.5 road dog spot and then Kyle Monangai, also questionable, with two IR bodies underneath. That's not depth, that's a prayer.

intro: Adam and Leif is the only unbeaten-on-unbeaten game on the board, and Adam gets the edge in a matchup where both rosters are deep enough that a single busted blocking assignment in the red zone decides it. Peter is the other 2-0 team walking into trouble, drawing a Logan squad that's favored despite an 0-2 start, which tells you more about Peter's lineup than it does about Logan's record. The widest gap is Kaleb over John, who has spent two weeks starting players whose NFL teams appear to be actively avoiding them.
